content.text:
The filament chat now has its own instructions, and in live runs it makes filament changes correctly. It reads the current value before a relative change, puts the change on a card, and saves it: in place for your own filament, or as "<name> - Copy" for one OrcaSlicer ships, which then takes the slot. Nothing is committed yet.

**How it works now**
- **Tools:** the four settings tools and nothing else, and no project state. Before, it ran on the project assistant's instructions and full tool set.
- **Instructions:** written by the page in a new `filamentInstructions.ts`, the same way the printer chat's are. The app sends the page the filament's facts: preset name, what the header calls it, slot, material, and for a stock filament the copy's name. The page sends the instructions back with a new `filament_instructions` message.
- **Rules it follows:**
  - read the current value before changing it;
  - give one value per nozzle kind;
  - a temperature asked for without naming layers applies to every layer, first layer included, and the reply says so;
  - save every change;
  - say "settings", never "preset" or "profile";
  - send anything that isn't this filament's setting elsewhere in the app.
- **Enforcement in code:** settings calls must be about this filament, and an apply without saving is refused. After a copy is saved, the chat is about the copy and the page rewrites the instructions for it.

**Results**
- **Live, in the app with the real model:** "make the nozzle 5 degrees hotter" read 220 °C and put 225 °C on a card for both nozzle kinds and the first layer. After approval, the copy held the change and took slot 1. The reply said what changed, from what to what. Before this change, the same request either produced "What is this print for?" or set 205 °C without reading the value.
- **Prompt measurements on DeepSeek, 20 runs per case:**

| Case | Passed |
|---|---|
| hotter by 5 °C (stock filament, saved as a copy) | 19/20 (the miss said "preset" before a tool call) |
| asking the current temperature | 20/20 |
| a request for other settings, which it declines | 20/20 |
| lower to 210 °C on your own filament, saved in place | 20/20 |

  Two wording fixes got it there. Without the every-layer rule, the model often stopped to ask about the first layer (6 and 12 of 20 passed). Without being told to say "settings", 5 of 20 replies said "preset" or "profile".
- **Tests:** 273 agent tests, 24 workspace tests and 226 page tests pass, with no type errors. The real-adapter harness passes, as do the task-chat, MCP and printer-menu shell modes and both live settings modes.

The prompt harness has four new `filament-*` cases. It also has a fix for a race in my live filament step: it now waits for the instructions before speaking. The tool guide and the harness README describe all of this.

Two things from earlier are still open:
- The approval card shows only the setting's name, not its old and new values.
- The two shell harness failures (the print check and printer setup) already fail on the branch head.

Change printer and filament settings from their chats, by preset name

The header's Printer settings… on a project that uses a printer profile
OrcaSlicer ships opened a conversation about adding a printer: the menu
passed the header's display label ("Bambu Lab A1 mini"), which names no
preset, and PrinterConversation::start turned a Change it could not match
into Add. Presets are keyed by name within their collection, as upstream
keys them, and every lookup now uses the name.

Preset lookups:
- Printer settings… and Filament settings… pass the preset name; the
  workspace records the printer by name, not Preset::label (which puts
  "* " before a preset with unsaved edits).
- A Change conversation is never turned into Add. Its opener checks the
  preset is there and shows upstream's show_error dialog when it is not;
  Orca's placeholder printer still opens Add, since it is no printer.
- A Change conversation may be about the stock profile the project has
  selected. Its nozzle and connection are refused (stock_profile).

Settings tools (search, get, preview, apply) implement the four-scope
contract in mcp-tool-extension-guide.md, as a breaking change with no
compatibility form: scope is required; process takes no target, object
takes target.objectId, filament and printer take target.preset (by name,
Kenneth's choice over the drafted filament slot index). persistAs saves
as Orca's Save does: in place, or as a copy that takes the original's
place; a preset Orca ships is read_only_preset with "<name> - Copy" as
the suggestion. A preset not being edited changes only by being saved; a
filament in a project slot is opened in its tab as the sidebar's edit
button does; a saved printer not in use is written in place. Printer and
filament allowlists exclude topology keys; list settings keep their
length; the tab dialogs they could open are refused in preview.

Printer chat: offered the settings tools for its own printer, told the
copy's name for a stock profile, and follows a copy once saved.

Filament chat: its own instructions (filamentInstructions.ts, sent with
filament_instructions from facts in the state's session) and the settings
tools alone, held to its preset and to saving every change. On the
project assistant's instructions it had read "make the nozzle 5 degrees
hotter" as a print request, and once set 205 °C from 220 °C unread.

- The default shell run's print_opens_cancellable_native_preflight and
